**What I did:** built a real `python3.12` venv, then ran `pip install -r requirements.txt` (and separately `pip install .` for the `setup.py install_requires` list) with no edits to any version specifier. Both are floor-only (`>=`) or unconstrained (`mistune`, `werkzeug`, `packaging`), so pip's resolver is free to pick whatever satisfies them.

Result: it resolved cleanly with zero conflicts, landing on Flask 3.1.3, Werkzeug 3.1.8, PyYAML 6.0.3, jsonschema 4.26.0, six 1.17.0, mistune 3.3.4, packaging 26.3 — all of which import and run under 3.12. I then installed flasgger itself (`pip install -e .`) into that same environment and confirmed `import flasgger` succeeds and its test suite runs (6/6 of the core tests pass; the only failures are 4 CLI tests broken by an unrelated Click `CliRunner(mix_stderr=...)` removal in test helper code — not an installability/resolution problem, and not one of the declared runtime dependencies).

I also stress-tested this by forcing each package down to its literal declared floor in isolation (e.g. `PyYAML==3.10`, `Werkzeug==0.7`) to see whether the *lower bound itself* is 3.12-safe — several floors do fail at runtime on 3.12 (`PyYAML` <5.1 hits `collections.Hashable` removal; old `Werkzeug` hits `dict.iteritems`). But since none of these are pinned with `==` or capped with `<`, that's irrelevant to actual resolvability: pip's default (highest-compatible) resolution never lands on those broken floors in practice, and the real end-to-end install/import/test run above confirms it doesn't. So no declared version constraint has to change for a move to 3.12 to work.
